text:
Dave: Uploaded an nsys snapshot — timeline shows repeated H2D memcpy bursts on stream 6 that line up with 2–3s latency spikes. Anyone seen host->device copies serializing kernels recently? screenshot: https://redwood-internal/trace/2440001

Sophia: interesting — do you see any KV-prefetch activity nearby? if the prefetch thread is issuing cudaMemcpyAsync on the default stream it can force serialization with other streams.

Li: default stream vs per-stream semantics are sneaky. async copies on the implicit stream can behave like a sync point w.r.t. other streams depending on API usage.

Dave: I'm pretty sure these are cudaMemcpyAsync from the prefetcher (pinned->device). nvtx markers show the copy group landing on stream 0x7 repeatedly. here's the profiling command i used:

```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt,nvtx --output=run2 --sample=cpu --timeout=120 
# trimmed flags for staging run
```

Mike: can you paste a small waterfall clip (start..end) where kernel waits for the memcpy? also double-check the host thread's state — i've seen kube CPU steals cause big host-side gaps.

Dave: pasted snippet from the timeline: memcpy starts at 1.24s on stream 3, transfers ~1.6MB, completes at 1.27s; the attention kernel on stream 1 doesn't launch until 1.36s. host thread that kicked off the memcpy shows a syscall block and then a 70–90ms sleep (sched_switch).

Sophia: that pattern smells like coalesced small-copy batching on the host thread. the batcher bundles a few small tensors into one host-side buffer then issues a single H2D. If the host side is preempted while building the buffer, the resulting big memcpy delays kernels. two mitigations: move copy assembly to a dedicated pinned thread/core or reduce max coalesce window.

tracebot: [auto] label added: perf/regression; captured run id=2440001234-run2; analyzers notified.

Li: also worth checking kernel selection paths — some new fused kernels pick different launch configs and may do CPU-side prep that blocks. if the kernel uses a host callback or cudaStreamAddCallback it could serialize more than expected.

Dave: quick repro plan posted: 1) nsys --sample=high on a single worker 2) disable KV prefetch to remove the prefetch memcpy 3) run with batcher.max_coalesce_ms=1 to avoid coalescing. anyone can help run step 2 on staging?

Mike: i'm on it. running disabling prefetche rflag now, and I'll lower the coalesce window. will report back with new timeline.

Sophia: also add a perfetto capture to include sched_switch events, that will nail whether the host thread is being preempted. look for frequent TASK_RUNNING->TASK_RUNNING gaps.

Dave: perfect — thanks. i'll post run2 trace clip and a trimmed nvprof snapshot in ~30m. if this repros we should consider pinning the prefetch thread to an isolated core and/or switching to cudaMemcpyAsync on a dedicated non-default stream. :thumbsup:
